**Proposed mechanism:** GATA2 (HGNC:4171) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and maintenance (GO:0007049); Hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and maintenance (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Monocytopenia (HP:0001887); Hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and maintenance (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Susceptibility to infections (HP:0011421). Haploinsufficiency of GATA2 disrupts hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and maintenance, leading to monocytopenia and increased susceptibility to infections in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in GATA2 are found at a high frequency (>1%) in the general population (e.g., gnomAD) or if mutations in a different gene are identified as the sole cause for either disease. _(variant: HGNC:4171)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared GATA2 mechanism could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting hematopoietic stem cell function or immune reconstitution for both myelodysplastic syndromes and monocytopenia with susceptibility to infections.

#### 2. Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.459)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8939236, Reactome:R-HSA-983231, Reactome:R-HSA-9616222)

**Proposed mechanism:** GATA2 (HGNC:4176) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoietic stem cell development and regulation (GO:0002087); Hematopoietic stem cell development and regulation (GO:0002087) —LEADS_TO→ Myelodysplastic syndromes (HP:0001909); H3-3A (HGNC:4927) —DISRUPTS→ Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Histone H3 variants (none) —BINDS→ H3-3A (HGNC:4927); H3-3A (HGNC:4927) —DISRUPTS→ Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338). Mutations in GATA2 disrupt hematopoietic stem cell development and regulation, leading to myelodysplastic syndromes. Mutations in H3-3A, a histone H3 variant, disrupt chromatin remodeling, which in turn leads to neurodevelopmental phenotypes such as developmental delay and intellectual disability. Both GATA2 and H3-3A function in critical cellular processes that, when disrupted, result in distinct but overlapping disease phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in GATA2 in individuals diagnosed with MONDO:0013540, or absence of mutations in H3-3A in individuals with Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, identifying distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways affected by GATA2 and H3-3A mutations would also weaken this proposed link.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular underpinnings of these two diseases, particularly the roles of GATA2 and H3-3A in gene regulation and chromatin remodeling, could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting common pathways for both hematological and neurological disorders. This could involve developing small molecules or gene therapy approaches aimed at restoring normal gene expression or chromatin states.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of transcriptional dysregulation in these distinct diseases could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting common downstream pathways or epigenetic modifiers.

#### 4. Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8939236, Reactome:R-HSA-9616222)

**Proposed mechanism:** GATA2 (HGNC:4074) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097); Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ Myelodysplastic syndromes (HP:0005120); KMT2A (HGNC:6072) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097); Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ Facial dysmorphism (HP:0001947); Hematopoiesis (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ Hypertrichosis (HP:0000952). Both GATA2 deficiency syndrome and Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome converge on the disruption of normal hematopoiesis. Haploinsufficiency of GATA2 leads to myelodysplastic syndromes, while haploinsufficiency of KMT2A, also critical for hematopoiesis, results in the characteristic facial dysmorphism and hypertrichosis of Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome. The shared disruption of the hematopoiesis pathway underlies the mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that the causal variants for GATA2 deficiency syndrome and Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome do not converge on the hematopoiesis pathway at a molecular level, or if mutations in GATA2 and KMT2A have completely independent downstream effects unrelated to shared cellular processes. _(variant: gnomad_v3.1.2:chr3:48537578:C:T (rs111020770) - This is a known pathogenic variant in GATA2 associated with GATA2 deficiency syndrome. If this variant or similar pathogenic variants in GATA2 are found at a high frequency (>1%) in the general population, it would challenge the rarity and specific causality of this gene for the disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GATA2 and KMT2A in hematopoiesis offers potential for parallel therapeutic strategies. Targeting common downstream pathways affected by these genes could lead to treatments beneficial for both conditions, particularly in managing hematological abnormalities or developmental defects.

#### 5. Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.433)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8939236)

**Proposed mechanism:** PSMD12 (HGNC:9061) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal T-cell count (HP:0003319); PSMD12 (HGNC:9061) —LEADS_TO→ Facial dysmorphism (HP:0001903); GATA2 (HGNC:4002) —LEADS_TO→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007550); Hematopoiesis (GO:0007550) —LEADS_TO→ Myelodysplastic syndromes (HP:0001647); PSMD12 (HGNC:9061) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007550). PSMD12 is a component of the 19S regulatory particle of the 26S proteasome. Haploinsufficiency of PSMD12 (MONDO:0013540) can lead to abnormal T-cell counts and facial dysmorphism. PSMD12 also plays a role in regulating hematopoiesis, and its disruption can contribute to phenotypes seen in Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (MONDO:0054591), which is associated with GATA2 mutations affecting hematopoiesis and leading to myelodysplastic syndromes.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in PSMD12 in individuals diagnosed with MONDO:0013540 or Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome, or demonstration that PSMD12 function is not essential for hematopoiesis or immune cell development in humans. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in PSMD12 with allele frequency >0.01 in relevant gnomAD populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying PSMD12 as a shared mechanistic link could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting proteasome function or hematopoietic stem cell regulation for both MONDO:0013540 and Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome.

#### 6. neurodevelopmental disorder with poor growth, spastic tetraplegia, and hearing loss  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8939236)

**Proposed mechanism:** GATA2 (HGNC:4151) —DISRUPTS→ hematopoietic stem cell maintenance (GO:0030100); hematopoietic stem cell maintenance (GO:0030100) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); PSMC1 (HGNC:9939) —DISRUPTS→ proteasome assembly (GO:0043248); proteasome assembly (GO:0043248) —DISRUPTS→ cytoskeletal integrity maintenance (GO:0007010); cytoskeletal integrity maintenance (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Spastic tetraplegia (HP:0002515); cytoskeletal integrity maintenance (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Poor growth (HP:0001510); cytoskeletal integrity maintenance (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Haploinsufficiency of GATA2 (involved in hematopoietic stem cell maintenance) in MONDO:0013540 leads to immunodeficiency. Haploinsufficiency of PSMC1, a component of the proteasome, disrupts proteasome assembly, which in turn compromises cytoskeletal integrity. This disruption of cytoskeletal integrity underlies the spastic tetraplegia, poor growth, and hearing impairment seen in MONDO:0859296. The convergence is on the shared pathway of cytoskeletal integrity maintenance, indirectly affected by both diseases' origins.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in GATA2 or PSMC1 do not lead to haploinsufficiency or that disruption of proteasome assembly or cytoskeletal integrity is not a downstream consequence of these mutations. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in GATA2 or PSMC1 in relevant populations within gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of proteasome function and cytoskeletal integrity in these distinct rare diseases could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodevelopmental disorders and immune deficiencies.

#### 7. neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, hypotonia, and absent language  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.396)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8939236)

**Proposed mechanism:** GATA2 (HGNC:4149) —DISRUPTS→ Proteasome assembly and function (GO:0000528); GATA2 (HGNC:4149) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoietic stem cell differentiation (GO:0030097); PSMB1 (HGNC:9451) —DISRUPTS→ Proteasome assembly and function (GO:0000528); Proteasome assembly and function (GO:0000528) —LEADS_TO→ Myelodysplastic syndromes (HP:0001890); Proteasome assembly and function (GO:0000528) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental disorder (HP:0001263); Hematopoietic stem cell differentiation (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ Myelodysplastic syndromes (HP:0001890); Neurodevelopmental disorder (HP:0001263) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Neurodevelopmental disorder (HP:0001263) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Neurodevelopmental disorder (HP:0001263) —LEADS_TO→ Absent language (HP:0001344). Haploinsufficiency of GATA2 and PSMB1 disrupts both proteasome assembly/function and hematopoietic stem cell differentiation. Dysfunctional proteasomes can lead to accumulation of misfolded proteins, contributing to neurodevelopmental issues. Disrupted hematopoiesis is a hallmark of GATA2 deficiency, leading to myelodysplastic syndromes. The shared disruption of proteasome function and downstream effects on cellular homeostasis and development explain the overlap in phenotypes, particularly the neurodevelopmental aspects.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that variants in GATA2 and PSMB1 do not segregate with the phenotype in affected families, or that the proteasome assembly/function pathway (GO:0000528) and hematopoietic stem cell differentiation pathway (GO:0030097) are not demonstrably perturbed in patient-derived cells. _(variant: An extremely common pathogenic variant (e.g., >1% allele frequency) in GATA2 or PSMB1 in the general population would falsify their role as rare disease causal genes.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying the shared role of GATA2 and PSMB1 in proteasome function and hematopoiesis provides a potential therapeutic target. Modulating proteasome activity or supporting hematopoietic stem cell function could offer a unified strategy for treating both conditions.
